title: This Shark Kills With a Tail Whip at 50 mph (and Boils the Water)

scenes.text: This shark whips prey to death at 50 miles an hour.
The thresher shark. Its tail is as long as the rest of its body.
It swims into a ball of sardines, flips its tail over its head, and cracks it down.
The tip hits 50 miles an hour. So fast that bubbles tear out of the water.
One strike lasts a third of a second and stuns seven fish.
Scientists only filmed it in 2013. A whip. At 50 miles an hour.

description:
Thresher sharks hunt by whipping their enormous tails over their heads to stun schooling sardines.
A 2013 study filmed the behaviour off Pescador Island in the Philippines: the tail tip averaged about 30 miles an hour and the fastest strike reached nearly 50, so quick that gas bubbles cavitated out of the water. A single strike lasted around 0.4 seconds and killed up to seven sardines.
What's the strangest way an animal hunts? Comment below.
first_comment: Only about one in three overhead slaps actually catches anything, but when it works the shark gets a whole meal in one hit. Which shark would you least like to meet?
